overview: An ice maker that has power but makes no ice almost always comes down to water not reaching the mold or the ice maker module itself failing. Work from the cheapest, most common cause to the most involved.

causes.title: Clogged or overdue water filter
causes.detail: A filter past its 6-month life restricts water flow enough to starve the ice maker. This is the most common and cheapest fix, so rule it out first.

causes.title: Failed water inlet valve
causes.detail: The inlet valve opens to let water into the ice maker. If it is clogged or the solenoid has failed, no water reaches the mold even though the ice maker runs.

causes.title: Defective ice maker assembly
causes.detail: If water reaches the unit but it won't cycle, harvest, or eject cubes, the ice maker module itself has likely failed and should be replaced as a unit.

causes.title: Freezer too warm or control board fault
causes.detail: The freezer must hold near 0 F to make ice. If temperatures are erratic across the fridge, the temperature control board may be at fault.

quick_checks: Confirm the ice maker is switched ON and the wire arm or feeler is down.
Make sure the freezer is at or below 0 F (-18 C).
Check that the household water supply valve behind the fridge is fully open.
Replace the water filter if it is older than 6 months.

overview: A fridge that runs but won't get cold usually has a defrost or airflow problem, or a door that no longer seals.

causes.title: Worn door gasket
causes.detail: A torn or hardened gasket lets cold air leak out, so the compressor runs constantly but the box never gets cold.

causes.title: Failed defrost thermostat
causes.detail: If the defrost system fails, frost builds on the evaporator and blocks airflow, leaving the fridge warm while the freezer stays cold.

causes.title: Temperature control board fault
causes.detail: Erratic or no cooling across the appliance can point to the main control board.

quick_checks: Verify the temperature setting hasn't been bumped.
Check that vents inside the fridge and freezer are not blocked by food.
Listen for the evaporator fan and compressor running.
Inspect the door gasket for tears or gaps.

overview: Standing water at the end of a cycle points to a blocked or failed drain path. Clear obstructions first, then test the pump.

causes.title: Clogged filter
causes.detail: A filter packed with food debris restricts drainage and is the first thing to clean or replace.

causes.title: Failed drain pump
causes.detail: If the filter is clear but the dishwasher hums without emptying, the drain pump motor has likely failed.

quick_checks: Clean the filter at the bottom of the tub.
Check the drain hose for kinks behind the dishwasher.
Confirm the garbage disposal knockout plug was removed if recently installed.
Run the disposal to clear the shared drain line.

overview: Poor cleaning is usually a water-flow problem: something is blocking spray pressure or trapping food, or detergent isn't being released.

causes.title: Clogged filter
causes.detail: A dirty filter redeposits food on dishes and should be cleaned or replaced first.

causes.title: Cracked or clogged spray arm
causes.detail: If the spray arm holes are blocked or the arm is cracked, water pressure drops and dishes stay dirty.

causes.title: Detergent not dispensing
causes.detail: If the dispenser door won't open mid-cycle, detergent never reaches the dishes.

causes.title: Upper rack sitting too low
causes.detail: A failed rack adjuster can let the upper rack block the spray tower so top dishes don't get cleaned.

quick_checks: Clean the filter and check the spray arms for clogs.
Run hot water at the sink before starting the cycle.
Use rinse aid and fresh detergent.
Make sure tall items aren't blocking the spray arm rotation.

overview: Leaks during a cycle most often trace to a worn door seal or a loose spray arm spraying past the gasket.

causes.title: Worn door seal
causes.detail: A cracked or flattened door gasket lets water escape the front of the tub during the wash.

quick_checks: Inspect the door gasket for tears, gaps, or food buildup.
Confirm the dishwasher is level so water pools toward the sump.
Avoid overloading so the door can close fully.
Use only dishwasher detergent to prevent oversudsing.
